nyciml-2005-06-spring-sophfrosh-01.prompt: Compute the smallest positive integral factor of $3476$ that contains two digits.

nyciml-2005-06-spring-sophfrosh-03.prompt: Sho the Great was born and died, respectively, in years that were the perfect squares of consecutive positive integers. If he died on his birthday at the age of $55$, compute the year he was born.

nyciml-2005-06-spring-sophfrosh-04.prompt: If $r$ is one more than the sum of the squares of three consecutive odd integers; compute the greatest common divisor of all possible $r$.

nyciml-2005-06-spring-sophfrosh-05.prompt: If $\dfrac{x+2}{x+1}$ and its reciprocal are both integers, compute $x$.

nyciml-2005-06-spring-sophfrosh-06.prompt: Gee Hoon has ten cards, labeled consecutively $1, 2, 3, \ldots, 10$. He chooses three of the cards and gets a sum of $14$. Compute the number of different sets of cards for which this could happen.

nyciml-2005-06-spring-sophfrosh-07.prompt: Three positive integers are added two at a time giving sums of $105$, $128$, and $141$. Compute the smallest integer.

nyciml-2005-06-spring-sophfrosh-08.prompt: In an isosceles right triangle, the difference between the length of the hypotenuse and the length of a leg is $5$. Compute the length of the hypotenuse.
nyciml-2005-06-spring-sophfrosh-08.reviewNote: Official key gives 5*sqrt(2)+5, which is the leg length (the official solution solves for the leg and stops). The hypotenuse is 10+5*sqrt(2); stored that.

nyciml-2005-06-spring-sophfrosh-09.prompt: Brad and Angela are planning their wedding. There is a charge to rent the room where they will have the party plus an additional charge per guest. If there are $400$ people at the party, the total cost will be \$130,000. If there are $280$ people at the party, the total cost will be \$97,000. Compute the cost of the party if $100$ people attend.

nyciml-2005-06-spring-sophfrosh-10.prompt: Paul is older than $9$ and younger than $100$. If he subtracts the product of the digits of his age from his age, he gets $19$. Compute all the possible ages that Paul can be.

nyciml-2005-06-spring-sophfrosh-11.prompt: Three cuts are made through a large cube to create $8$ identical smaller cubes. If the total surface area of the large cube is $13$, compute the total surface area of the small cubes.

nyciml-2005-06-spring-sophfrosh-12.prompt: The planet Jostern has a year that contains only $8$ days. If three residents of Jostern are in a room, compute the probability that at least two were born on the same day of the year.

nyciml-2005-06-spring-sophfrosh-13.prompt: The Chess club shares its winnings. The first place finisher gets half of the money, the second place finisher gets $3/4$ of the remainder of the money, then the third place finisher gets $3/4$ of the money that now remains, and then the two fourth place finishers equally share what is left. If the fourth place finishers each got \$5, compute the total amount of money that was won by the club members.

nyciml-2005-06-spring-sophfrosh-14.prompt: $(2x + 3)^{x^2 - 3x + 2} = 1$. Compute all possible real values of $x$ for which this is true.

nyciml-2005-06-spring-sophfrosh-15.prompt: If $k$ is a natural number and $k(k + 1)$ is divided by $7$, compute all possible remainders.

nyciml-2005-06-spring-sophfrosh-16.prompt: Two sides of a triangle measure $2$ and $7$ and the length of the third side of the triangle is the same as the area of the triangle (without regards to units). Compute the area of the triangle.

nyciml-2005-06-spring-sophfrosh-18.prompt: The number of water lilies in a pond increases at a constant rate. Mrs. Carp released fish into the pond and after $96$ days, they have eaten all of the water lilies (those that were there at first and those that grew in the $96$ days.) The fish eat the water lilies at a constant rate. $70$ fish would have taken $24$ days to eat all of the lilies and $30$ fish would have taken $60$ days to eat all of the lilies, compute the number of fish that Mrs. Carp released into the pond.
